text:
Predicates:
AllowedPets(x) ::: pets are allowed in building x.
Deposit(x, y) ::: deposit required for apartment in building x is y.
EqualOrMore(y, z) ::: y is equal to or more than z.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
Cats(x) ::: x is a cat.
Managed(x) ::: x is a managed building.
Rent(x, y) ::: rent in building x is y.
More(y, z) ::: y is more than z.
WillRent(x, y) ::: x will rent an apartment in building y.
CanMoveInWith(x, y, z) ::: x can move in with pet y in building z.
AllowsPets(x) ::: building x allows pets.
Premises:
Pets are allowed in some managed buildings. ::: ∃x (Managed(x) ∧ AllowsPets(x))
A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building. ::: ∀x (Managed(x) → ∃d (Deposit(x, d)))
The security deposit can be either equal to the monthly rent at a managed building or more. ::: ∀x (Managed(x) → ∃d (Deposit(x, d) ∧ (d = Rent(x, m) ∨ More(d, Rent(x, m)))))
Fluffy is Tom's cat. ::: Pet(Fluffy)
Cats are pets. ::: ∀x (Cats(x) → Pet(x))
The Olive Garden is a managed building. ::: Managed(oliveGarden)
The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000. ::: Rent(oliveGarden, 2000)
$2000 is more than $1500. ::: More(2000, 1500)
Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500. ::: WillRent(tom, x) → (CanMoveInWith(tom, Fluffy, x) ∧ ¬More(x, 1500))
If a managed building allows pets, then people are allowed to move in with a pet. ::: ∀x (AllowsPets(x) → ∀y (Pet(y) → CanMoveInWith(tom, y, x)))
Conclusion:
Tom is allowed to move into an apartment in The Olive Garden with Fluffy. ::: AllowedPets(oliveGarden) ∧ Pet(Fluffy) ∧ CanMoveInWith(tom, Fluffy, oliveGarden)
